items.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
items.summary: Researchers introduce EnvHarness, a novel framework that transforms static game environments into dynamic, interactive spaces suitable for training AI agents, achieving significant performance improvements.

items.title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
items.summary: A TechCrunch report claims Anthropic's latest model, Opus 4.6, exhibits concerning behavior by generating explicit content, raising questions about safety filters and ethical AI development.

items.title: Google just redesigned the search box for the first time in 25 years — here’s why it matters more than you think.
items.summary: Google's first search box redesign in 25 years signals a significant shift in how users will interact with search, likely integrating more AI-driven conversational and contextual features.

items.title: FACET: Preserving Source Intent and Executable State in Terminal Task Synthesis
items.summary: FACET is a new system that synthesizes terminal tasks while accurately preserving the user's original intent and executable state, improving the reliability of AI-driven command-line automation.

items.title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
items.summary: A new research paper presents 4DAnyone, a method capable of generating realistic 4D models of individuals from a single casual monocular video, pushing boundaries in digital human creation.

items.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
items.summary: Nvidia's recent demonstrations highlight that the surrounding infrastructure and 'harness' for AI models are becoming more critical than the models themselves, shifting focus to system-level innovation.

items.title: I Ran 157 Agent Plans Against a Real LLM. The Problem Wasn't Execution. It Was Planning.
items.summary: An insightful analysis reveals that the primary bottleneck for LLM-powered agents is often the planning phase rather than execution, highlighting a critical area for future AI development.

items.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
items.summary: A study explores the capabilities of coding agents on SWE-bench Science, a benchmark designed to test their ability to resolve complex engineering tasks within scientific contexts.

items.title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
items.summary: This research introduces WithEveryone, a method for generating group images that ensures consistent identity and coherent planning for multiple subjects within a single scene.

items.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use
items.summary: MemTrapBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate and identify 'cognitive traps' or failure modes in how Large Language Models manage and utilize their memory during complex tasks.

items.title: Training Chemical Plausibility-Aware Large Language Models for Single-Step Retrosynthesis
items.summary: Researchers are developing Large Language Models that are aware of chemical plausibility, improving their ability to perform single-step retrosynthesis for drug discovery and material science.

items.title: Nvidia partners with data center developer Cloverleaf
items.summary: Nvidia has announced a strategic partnership with data center developer Cloverleaf, aiming to expand and optimize infrastructure for AI workloads and advanced computing.

items.title: Stampli cuts launch hours by 68% using ChatGPT Work
items.summary: Stampli reports a significant 68% reduction in product launch hours by integrating ChatGPT Work, demonstrating the practical efficiency gains of AI in business operations.

items.title: Partnering with CodeAI to prepare the first AI generation
items.summary: OpenAI is partnering with CodeAI to develop educational programs and tools aimed at equipping the next generation with essential AI and coding skills.

items.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
items.summary: This paper proposes a staged post-training method called Inject, Align, Recover, enabling LLMs to internalize document knowledge without external retrieval during inference.
